method.name: Stepwise
method.label: Stepwise 2006
method.description: The Stepwise 2006 method as SimaPro's 1.09 export ships it: 19 categories carried forward to quality-adjusted life years and to 2003 euros, with the IPCC 2021 global warming numbers and a corrected nature occupation model.

implementations.name: brightway-flows
implementations.source: ours, derived from the deciding implementations, each factor saying how

categories.name: Acidification
categories.description: Acidifying emissions, counted as the area of ecosystem left above its critical load and so unprotected.

indicator.source: EDIP 2003, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from: 'area of unprotected ecosystem = m2 UES'. Hauschild & Potting (2005), Spatial differentiation in life cycle impact assessment -- the EDIP2003 methodology, Danish EPA Environmental News 80.

categories.name: Economic costs
categories.description: Costs the method prices directly, in 2003 euros. The one category whose indicator is money rather than an environmental quantity.

indicator.source: Stepwise 2006 itself, in the method comment of its v1.09 SimaPro export: it 'uses exclusively EURO2003 for economic costs assessment (life cycle costing)'.

categories.name: Ecotoxicity, aquatic
categories.description: Substances released that poison life in fresh water, as the kilograms of triethylene glycol into water that would do the same harm.

indicator.source: IMPACT 2002+ v2.1, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from, whose reference substance is 'kg Triethylene glycol into water-eq'. Jolliet et al. (2003), Int J LCA 8(6):324-330; Humbert et al. (2005), IMPACT 2002+ User Guide.

categories.name: Ecotoxicity, terrestrial
categories.description: Substances released that poison life in soil, as the kilograms of triethylene glycol into soil that would do the same harm.

indicator.source: IMPACT 2002+ v2.1, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from, whose reference substance is 'kg Triethylene glycol into soil-eq'. Jolliet et al. (2003), Int J LCA 8(6):324-330; Humbert et al. (2005), IMPACT 2002+ User Guide.

categories.name: Eutrophication, aquatic
categories.description: Nutrients reaching water and feeding the growth that strips it of oxygen, as the kilograms of nitrate with the same effect.

indicator.source: EDIP 2003, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from: nitrogen and phosphorus aggregated 'into an NO3- potential reflecting the amount of NO3- that would lead to the same potential eutrophication in aquatic systems'. Hauschild & Potting (2005), Spatial differentiation in life cycle impact assessment -- the EDIP2003 methodology, Danish EPA Environmental News 80.

categories.name: Eutrophication, terrestrial
categories.description: Nutrients reaching soil, counted on the same unprotected-ecosystem area scale as acidification.

indicator.source: EDIP 2003, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from: 'area of unprotected ecosystem = m2 UES'. Hauschild & Potting (2005), Spatial differentiation in life cycle impact assessment -- the EDIP2003 methodology, Danish EPA Environmental News 80.

categories.name: Global warming, fossil
categories.description: Warming from carbon that was locked underground, as the kilograms of carbon dioxide with the same effect.

indicator.source: Stepwise 2006 itself, in the method comment of its v1.09 SimaPro export: 'uses IPCC 2021 (IPCC's Sixth Assessment Report) GWP100 factors'. The words are the ones the JRC and the ecoinvent Centre use for the same quantity under EF 3.1.

categories.name: Global warming, non-fossil
categories.description: Warming from carbon that was in circulation already -- burnt wood, peat, waste -- kept apart from the fossil kind because the two are reported separately.

indicator.source: Stepwise 2006 itself, in the method comment of its v1.09 SimaPro export: 'uses IPCC 2021 (IPCC's Sixth Assessment Report) GWP100 factors'. The words are the ones the JRC and the ecoinvent Centre use for the same quantity under EF 3.1.

categories.name: Human toxicity, carcinogens
categories.description: Substances released that cause cancer in people, as the kilograms of vinyl chloride that would do the same harm.

indicator.source: IMPACT 2002+ v2.1, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from, whose reference substance is 'kg Chloroethylene into air-eq'. Jolliet et al. (2003), Int J LCA 8(6):324-330; Humbert et al. (2005), IMPACT 2002+ User Guide.

categories.name: Human toxicity, non-carc.
categories.description: Substances released that harm people without causing cancer, on the same vinyl chloride scale as the carcinogens.

indicator.source: IMPACT 2002+ v2.1, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from, whose reference substance is 'kg Chloroethylene into air-eq'. Jolliet et al. (2003), Int J LCA 8(6):324-330; Humbert et al. (2005), IMPACT 2002+ User Guide.

categories.name: Injuries, road or work
categories.description: Injuries on the road and at work, weighted to the equivalent number of fatal ones. Counted from the activity itself rather than from anything released.

indicator.source: Stepwise 2006 itself: 'The category indicator is ‘fatal-injury-equivalents’'. Weidema et al. (2008), Environmental improvement potentials of meat and dairy products, EUR 23491 EN, Annex II, section 13.3.1.

categories.name: Ionizing radiation
categories.description: Radioactivity released, as the becquerels of carbon-14 that would expose people to the same dose.

indicator.source: IMPACT 2002+ v2.1, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from, whose reference substance is 'Bq Carbon-14 into air-eq'. Jolliet et al. (2003), Int J LCA 8(6):324-330; Humbert et al. (2005), IMPACT 2002+ User Guide.

categories.name: Mineral extraction
categories.description: Minerals taken from the ground, counted as the extra energy a later extraction will need because this one lowered the ore grade.

indicator.source: IMPACT 2002+ v2.1, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from, which counts it in 'MJ surplus energy', the expected increase of the energy needed to extract lower-grade ores. Jolliet et al. (2003), Int J LCA 8(6):324-330; Humbert et al. (2005), IMPACT 2002+ User Guide.

categories.name: Nature occupation
categories.description: Land held out of nature, counted as the fraction of species that potentially disappear from a square metre for a year.

indicator.words: Potentially disappeared fraction of endemic species (PDF) over area and time
indicator.source: Stepwise 2006 itself, in the method comment of its v1.09 SimaPro export: 'the duration of area occupied (m2*years) multiplied with a severity score, representing the proportion of endemic species disappeared from that area'. The 'm2-equivalents arable land' of the 2008 documentation is the unit version 1.6 replaced.

categories.name: Non-renewable energy
categories.description: Energy taken from stocks that do not refill -- fossil carriers and uranium -- counted at the primary carrier.

indicator.source: IMPACT 2002+ v2.1, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from, which counts it in 'MJ total primary non-renewable energy'. Jolliet et al. (2003), Int J LCA 8(6):324-330; Humbert et al. (2005), IMPACT 2002+ User Guide.

categories.name: Ozone layer depletion
categories.description: Thinning of the stratospheric ozone layer, as the kilograms of trichlorofluoromethane with the same effect.

indicator.source: IMPACT 2002+ v2.1, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from, whose reference substance is 'kg CFC-11 into air-eq', the substance an ozone depletion potential is relative to. The words are the ones the JRC uses for the same quantity under EF 3.1. Jolliet et al. (2003), Int J LCA 8(6):324-330; Humbert et al. (2005), IMPACT 2002+ User Guide.

categories.name: Photochemical ozone, vegetat.
categories.description: Ground-level ozone formed from emitted organics, counted as the vegetation exposed to it: square metres times parts per million times hours.

indicator.words: Accumulated ozone exposure of vegetation above 40 ppb (AOT40)
indicator.source: EDIP 2003, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from: 'the AOT40, the accumulated exposure (duration times exceedance of threshold) above the threshold of 40 ppb times the area that is exposed'. Hauschild & Potting (2005), Spatial differentiation in life cycle impact assessment -- the EDIP2003 methodology, Danish EPA Environmental News 80.

categories.name: Respiratory inorganics
categories.description: Fine particles, and the gases that turn into them in the air, as the kilograms of PM2.5 people would breathe for the same harm.

indicator.source: IMPACT 2002+ v2.1, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from, whose reference substance is 'kg PM2.5 into air-eq'. Jolliet et al. (2003), Int J LCA 8(6):324-330; Humbert et al. (2005), IMPACT 2002+ User Guide.

categories.name: Respiratory organics
categories.description: Ground-level ozone formed from emitted organics, counted as the people exposed to it: persons times parts per million times hours.

indicator.words: Accumulated ozone exposure of people above 60 ppb (AOT60)
indicator.source: EDIP 2003, which Stepwise 2006 takes this category from: 'the AOT60, the accumulated exposure above the threshold of 60 ppb times the number of persons which are exposed'. Hauschild & Potting (2005), Spatial differentiation in life cycle impact assessment -- the EDIP2003 methodology, Danish EPA Environmental News 80.
